title: The world as dream
hook: a dream, a show, a bubble on water: the ninth Guru's pictures of a passing world

segments.voice: Yesterday, the traveler's hymns: O mind, take shelter. Your line was prayer on the road. Did you find your spot, and take the breath there? Day one thousand two hundred nineteen.

There's a half second, just after a vivid dream, when the dream is still the real world. The argument is still going. The house is still that strange house. Then the ceiling comes into focus, a car passes outside, and the whole thing drains away like water from a sink. Nothing in it was lost, because none of it was ever held. Near the end of the Guru Granth Sahib, Guru Tegh Bahadur keeps coming back to that half second. Again and again, his saloks hold up the world and say: look, a dream.
screen: `THE HALF SECOND AFTER A DREAM.` → `IT DRAINS AWAY.` → `THE GURU: LOOK, A DREAM.`

segments.voice: Two of his saloks, paraphrased. The first: know this world as a dream and a passing show; in it, Nanak, nothing is true except the Lord. The second: as a bubble rises on water and bursts, again and again, so the world is made; listen, friend, says Nanak. A dream. A show. A bubble. Three pictures of something real enough to see, and too quick to keep. Now, here's what the dream does not mean. It doesn't mean nothing matters. The same Guru stayed a householder, traveled to visit his Sikhs, and stood up for other people's faith with his life. You don't do that for a world you think is worthless. One way Sikhs read these saloks: the dream is real as a dream. People, work, love, all of it is worth doing. What's untrue is the idea that any of it will stay. The mistake isn't living in the dream. It's clutching at it, as if the bubble could be put in a pocket. And the cure the saloks point to isn't to tear the world down. It's to wake up. To notice, while you're still inside it, that the One who is true was there all along. That's why the carry says gently. A slammed alarm clock wakes you angry. A curtain opened slowly wakes you well. The Guru's saloks open the curtain one line at a time: a dream, a show, a bubble, and in all of it, the Lord. Then they keep you company as you get up and go about the day, a little lighter, holding things the way you'd hold a bubble. Carefully. Without squeezing.
screen: `A DREAM, A SHOW, A BUBBLE.` · `IT DOESN'T MEAN NOTHING MATTERS.` · `THE MISTAKE IS CLUTCHING.` · `A CURTAIN, NOT AN ALARM.` · then, large: `WAKE UP GENTLY.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: wake gently. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one thing you've been gripping hard. A plan, a worry, a grudge, a thing you want badly. Don't throw it away. Just look at it the way you'd look at a dream you're slowly waking from. Real while it lasts. Not forever. With each breath out, let the room come into focus around it, the way the ceiling does after a dream. If you pray, you can rest in Waheguru, the one the saloks call true, on each breath in. The bell holds the time.
The world as dream. In the ninth Guru's saloks, the world is a dream, a show, a bubble on water, and nothing in it stays except the Lord. Today's word.
Your line: wake up gently. Today, when you catch yourself clutching, notice the bubble, and loosen your fingers instead of squeezing. Day one thousand two hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: Guru Tegh Bahadur's saloks, with their images of the world as a dream and a bubble, are read near the close of a complete reading of the Guru Granth Sahib, including the readings families hold after a death.

fork.setup: you've just heard the ninth Guru's salok: know this world as a dream. what do you do with your day?
options: give up on it: none of it is real.
grip it harder before it disappears.
live it fully, holding it lightly, remembering the One.
fork.reveal: the Guru stayed a householder and served to the end. the saloks warn against clutching, not against living.

original.note: a dream; the ninth Guru's saloks ask us to know the world as a dream and a passing show.

trapdoor: what you thought: if the world is a dream, nothing matters.
what it means: the world is real while it lasts, but doesn't stay; the mistake is clutching.
what a scholar hears: dream, show and bubble return across the saloks of Mahala 9, each paired with the Lord as what is true.
